spec_title: ISS Veggie seed film placement into plant pillows
outcome: earth (1 g) PASS; orbit (0 g) PASS

program.spec_title: ISS Veggie seed film placement into plant pillows
warnings: No visible scale reference; object sizes and poses are estimates based on typical ISS hardware.

failure_classes.evidence: In orbit (0 g), the seed film packet was released 0.7 mm above the pocket rim (22.7 mm above pocket floor) at 16.9 mm/s and never settled, causing wait_until object_still to timeout after 2 s (patched to 10 s, still failed). The compiled program used a final approach height of 36 mm from the top of obj2, which left the object above the rim in zero-g. Patch 3 lowered the height to 13 mm (pocket floor level), allowing contact before release and passing both worlds.

reshoot.why: The video does not show the vertical position of the packet relative to the pillow rim during insertion, so the compiler defaulted to an approach height that works in gravity but not in zero-g.
reshoot.ask: Film a close-up side view (10–15 cm away) of the astronaut’s hand placing the seed film packet into the plant pillow, clearly showing the packet height above the pillow rim at the moment of release.

reshoot.why: The interview value (10 mm) may represent lateral clearance, not pocket depth; the actual pocket floor is 21.9 mm below the rim, which is needed to set the correct insertion height.
reshoot.ask: Ask the astronaut: ‘What is the distance from the top rim of the plant pillow pocket down to the pocket floor?’

open_risks: Real seed film packets are flexible and may deform, unlike the rigid box model.
The parallel-jaw gripper may not achieve the same secure grasp as a gloved hand, leading to slip or misalignment.
ISS vibrations and air currents could disturb the packet after release, especially in zero-g.
Pocket geometry (taper, lip) is not captured in the box primitive; real insertion may require angular alignment.
value.outcome: earth (1 g) PASS; orbit (0 g) PASS
